newsitem.title: CANADA: AWP does not rule out upping UGG bid.
newsitem.headline: AWP does not rule out upping UGG bid.

text.p: Alberta Wheat Poll would not rule out increasing it's C$172 million hostile takeover offer for United Grain Growers Ltd if a rival bid materializes, AWB's chief financial officer Geoff Southwood told Reuters.
"In terms of a counter (offer), if ConAgra Inc came along we'd have to look at it in the light of day," Southwood said in a phone interview from Grande Prairie, Alta.
Alberta Wheat Pool and Manitoba Pool Elevators on Thursday made a C$13.75 a share bid for all the remaining voting shares of UGG citing the threat of a U.S. multinational takeover of UGG.
UGG stock rose C$0.20 to a new high of C$14.45 on the Toronto Stock Exchange with 11,239 shares changing hands.
U.S. multinational ConAgra has been the most frequently cited potential suitor for a UGG takeover in the past year.
Unconfirmed trade rumours now have ConAgra and UGG in merger talks with ConAgra paying C$15 a share to acquire UGG. Officials at ConAgra declined comment.
UGG's chief executive was not available for comment.
"We do think, however, that paying as we are a 35 percent premium to where the market was before we started buying the stock is very, very fair to shareholders," Southwood said.

Equity analysts said UGG's stock rise suggested Canadian agricultural assets were undervalued and commodity analysts said they believed the pools' bid for UGG was to stave off any further incursion into their provinces by rival Saskatchewan Wheat Pool.

Asked whether fears that SWP would acquire UGG had prompted their bid, Southwood replied: "It's possible and, of course, a strong competitor coming into Alberta or Manitoba would be a competitive threat."
Canadian Bond Rating Service placed UGG on its creditwatch list on Friday.
